title: Meal List Boundaries
user: A household planning meals for more than one home or pickup context who needs a weekly menu to produce the right shopping list without leaking one household's items into another.

evidence.quote_or_summary: The author of a local-first family meal planner receives a direct reply that this is an active pain for the commenter.
A Tandoor user has two homes and two lists but cannot scope each Home Assistant connector to only its own household's list.

recurrence: The need appears in both a local-first meal-planning launch and a detailed multi-home request; meal plans repeatedly cross household, store, and pickup boundaries.
current_workaround: Duplicate recipes/lists, manually deselect items, or maintain separate chats and shopping apps per household.
incumbents_and_gap: Mealie, Tandoor, Paprika, and AnyList cover recipes and lists, but list ownership/boundaries are usually a sync setting rather than a visible planning primitive.
smallest_useful_product: A local-first weekly board that assigns each meal and ingredient to a named household/list, generates separate printable or shareable lists, and records a simple 'bought' state. Non-goals: recipe scraping, delivery ordering, price comparison, and cloud accounts.
success_measure: At least 80% of pilot weeks produce two or more correctly separated lists with no manually copied ingredient between them.
monetization: one-time — families need a durable household utility, not a recurring charge for a grocery checklist.
constraints: Local export/import and QR handoff must work without a central account; avoid retailer integrations and retain no dietary or location data.
why_distinct: The primary object is a boundary-aware handoff from plan to the right buyer, not a generic recipe manager.
